45:**This is the first question of the interview.** It determines every later one: a product interview asks about first value and auth walls, a website interview asks about competitors and conversion goals. Asked in the wrong order you produce an interview that does not fit what the user has.
55:      Lenses: clarity · conversion · trust · icp · technical · seo · aeo · compare
59:      Runs (b) on the site, then (a) on the product. Two captures.
86:**⚑ The conversion goal.** *"What should a visitor do next?"* — sign up, book a call, read the docs, buy, join a list.
88:> Without it the `conversion` lens has no target and degrades into generic CTA advice. If the user genuinely does not know, record `conversion_goal: null` and tell them `conversion` will report mechanics only.
109:  clarity       can a visitor say what this is, who it's for, what to do next
110:  conversion    is the next step obvious at every scroll depth
111:  trust         proof, pricing transparency, who's behind it, data handling
116:  seo           crawlability, meta, canonical, structured data, sitemap
117:  aeo           schema.org, answer blocks, entity clarity, llms.txt
129:**`icp` scores whichever captures the run has** — a visit, a journey, or both — and the report says which. It is strongest on *both* (assessment type c). On a website run it adds Shape V-ICP, a three-to-five-minute sweep of pricing, proof, integrations and "for whom" pages, to each visit; say so.
131:**Say the cost out loud after they choose.** Adding a lens *within a mode you are already running* is nearly free — it scores evidence already captured. Adding a *mode* means another pass. `clarity + conversion + trust` is **one** visit; `clarity + seo` is **two** captures in different modes. Users routinely assume more lenses means proportionally more time; the surprise runs the other way.
182:If yes, per objective capture **two** things, in the user's own words:
195:- **Captured now, before capture.** An objective the persona never pursued cannot be scored honestly afterwards.
269:  (b) balanced    opus  → ux, content, onboarding, clarity, conversion,
270:      ← default            trust, icp, compare
271:                  sonnet → bugs, seo, aeo, technical
283:**Why balanced splits where it does:** `ux` and `content` ask a model to judge whether something is *good*, and a weaker model produces findings that are plausible and wrong — the most expensive failure mode, because a wrong P0 costs more than a missed P2. `bugs`, `seo` and `aeo` check observable facts against a rubric: was there a console error, is there a canonical tag, is there valid schema.org. The framework carries those.
409:Record them verbatim. Exclusions are applied at **scoring** time, not capture — the traversal still records what it sees, the analyst drops it. That distinction matters: an excluded thing that blocks the persona still explains why they got stuck.
424:Goal          "<conversion goal>"                       (website only)
426:Lenses        Mode A-visit → clarity, conversion, trust
427:              Mode C       → seo
437:Captures      3 × Mode A-visit traversal  (25 min cap each)
444:              scoring     balanced — opus: clarity, conversion, trust
445:                                     sonnet: seo
456:The **captures vs. scoring** split is the line that teaches the architecture. Keep it.
491:| Running `conversion` with no goal | It degrades into generic CTA advice indistinguishable from a real finding |

content.text:
**2 captures.**

| # | Mode | Serves | Persona |
|---|------|--------|---------|
| 1 | **Mode A-visit** (persona traversal of example-nimbus-notes.test) | clarity, conversion, trust | your one persona |
| 2 | **Mode C** (crawl — no session, no persona) | seo | none |

The arithmetic: captures are counted per **mode**, not per lens. `clarity`, `conversion` and `trust` all score the *same* recorded visit, so they cost one traversal between them — adding the second and third lens there is essentially free. `seo` needs page-level markup facts (titles, canonicals, structured data, sitemap, robots) that a persona visit doesn't collect, so it's a separate pass in a different mode. Hence 1 visit + 1 crawl = 2.

Scoring is four lens passes over those two captures — that's a separate step from capture and doesn't add browser time.

Two things that would change the number, for when you're ready:
- **More personas** → one additional Mode A-visit each (the crawl stays at 1 regardless).
- **Adding `aeo`** → free, it rides the same Mode C crawl. Adding `technical` → +1 (Mode B). Adding `compare` → the full set repeats per competitor site.

Nothing has been started, and I haven't run the interview.
